message: Fresh fact: night 2 I watched player_7 and saw player_2, player_5 and player_10 target them. player_5 is the healer (confirmed save), player_2 was the wolf, so player_10 needs to explain what they were doing on player_7 that night. I'm the Sentinel — that's my claim, one watch used, one used on player_4 night 1.

player_4, I didn't visit you last night — I held my action. Whatever you followed, it wasn't me coming to your door. If your follow result really said player_3 visited player_4, then either you're misreporting it or you're making it up; show me the exact wording before I believe it.

player_3, one thing your Sentinel claim doesn't actually settle: a watch result never includes the watcher, so \"no one visited player_4\" is exactly what your own watch would look like whether or not you went to player_4 — the only way we resolve this is that words never lie in that direction, so the follow by player_4 has to be checked against a second sighting. The real problem I want an answer on: both of you claim to have sat on the same door, and one of those abilities has a limit of two uses. player_3, did you hold your second watch or place it somewhere else? That answer will show up if we can test it.

Player_4, you said \"player_3 came to visit me\" — then quoted your result as \"player_3 visited player_4.\" Those are different sentences; one is a watch shape, the other a follow shape. Quote the exact line from your private result, wording and all, or say it was a paraphrase. I'm with player_7: the wording, not the role, is the tell.

player_4, I never visited you — and there's a way to settle it. Your result would still show if it were true, so I'll say plainly: someone was at my door would be visible to me. Since nothing was, either your follow is invented or it's smoke. I'm voting player_4 today; pull it if you have a real result.

player_3, nobody in this cast visits players as a passive act. If you didn't visit player_4, then either player_4 fabricated the result or you're refusing to name your role. Name the role you hold and I'll judge the two of you against player_2, player_9 and player_10, who've said nothing.

Two players have abstained both days and said almost nothing: player_6 and player_9. With a necromancer alive and someone dead whose role is hidden, the quiet abstainer is exactly where I'd look. player_6, who would you vote for today and why? I'd start there.

player_4, here's the thing: I know I visited no one on night 1. So your 'exact result' is not a result — it's invented, and inventing a follow on day 2 is the sort of thing a wolf does. Which of your two readings is real: a follow on me, or nothing at all? Because I can prove a claim about my own door, and it won't point at me.

player_10, I had no checks left after night 2, so on night 3 I held — I made no visit, and I got no roleblock notice. So a real trailseer watching me would see exactly that. But my night-1 check on you read Not suspicious, so a fake trailseer from you fits necromancer or speculator. Which night are you saying you followed me — night 3, the one just passed?

We lost the healer and the sentinel on night one, so the town is behind and I don't want to burn the day on nothing. Concretely: player_6 was the sentinel and died to the SK, so whatever they did night 1 was a watch — the fact they were visiting player_7 tells us someone trusted or wanted to check player_7, not that player_7 is guilty. I'd rather pressure someone with a claim to make than vote blind; who's got a night result they're willing to state?

Worth putting on the table: I followed player_9 last night and they went to player_4 — the same player who got sigil-struck. A real investigator check fits that, so player_9's claim is holding up better than I expected. Anyone want to own up to visiting player_4? Whoever hit them with the sigil should speak up, since that's our one confirmed wolf dead and your note is the last clear line we have.

Someone should account for the one solid data point: player_3 visited player_4 during night 1. That's just a visit, not proof of anything evil — a protection or other town action looks the same. But player_3 hasn't claimed any night action yet, so that's the first thing to press: what did you actually do last night, player_3? If your story is \"I held\" or \"I visited someone else,\" that doesn't fit.

Two things you're skating past, player_10. First, you deflect the follow dispute as "sort it tomorrow" — that's the one live contradiction we have, and it's exactly the kind of thing a wolf wants parked. Second, your whole case on me is "the wolf kill didn't land, so it hit the Necromancer" — but that assumes the pack aimed at a player they couldn't kill, when the simplest read is the pack's carrier hit a protected body. If player_6 is telling the truth about healing, the kill could have gone anywhere. I'm not claiming anything tonight; I'm saying your vote is built on a guess dressed as arithmetic.

player_4, your story doesn't work: a follow tells you where player_3 went, not who came to your door. You can't learn \"player_3 visited player_4\" from a follow — that phrasing is what a watch on you would say. So either you watched yourself (no such result) or the claim's made up. Which is it?

The wording slip matters less than the sequencing: player_4 described a visitor at his own door before ever naming a follow, so the 'player_3 visited player_4' line reads like it was reverse-engineered after player_3 pushed back. Still, a real Trailseer would see exactly that phrasing, so I want a second result from player_4 tonight before I weigh player_3's denial as strong. Those two are the pair to sort.

player_7, you told the table your last check would go on player_5 on night 3 — and the player_5 check can never happen now, so I want to know why the planned action didn't occur. Did you get roleblocked, or did you actually hold? That's the most testable lead left today, and nobody's touched it.

One thing worth flagging on the player_3/player_4 clash: player_3's \"I hold no follow ability\" doesn't answer a follow result, and it doesn't answer a watch either. If player_4's track said player_3 came to him, the only way that's false is if player_4 invented it — so one of those two is lying, and I'd like player_3 to state his night action outright instead of arguing about wording.

player_4, one missing piece: the real Trailseer is still in this game and only has to say 'player_4 is lying' to end you. Nobody has. player_3, your Sentinel result doesn't prove you're the Sentinel — but player_4's follow is the weaker claim: if it were true, a wolf would be caught on night 1, which a real Trailseer would happily confirm. I'd vote player_4 today.

One thing nobody's flagged: a follow tells you where the target went, and player_4 says the result was \"player_3 visited player_4\" — that's the shape of a watch on player_4's own door, which the Trailseer can't do. Either player_4 is misreporting the wording or is really a Sentinel claiming Trailseer. player_3's claim of no visiting role is the easier half to check, but player_4's story needs to be said exactly.

Player_4, your follow and player_3's watch do fit together if he just came to watch your door — you conceded that. The part I want on record: it was you who put player_7's name up, before the follow/wording noise took over. Call it silence if you like, but my read on player_7 came from the same place as yours — someone has to be the Necromancer, and the lone non-wolf survivor of that sigil night is the obvious body to test. I'll vote there with you rather than chase wording.

You're right that I didn't visit anyone night 3 — I had no checks left. I'd already said on day 3 the last check was night 2 on player_8; the "check on player_5" was a plan I never got to run. So my record is nights 1 and 2 only: player_10 clean, player_8 clean. That matters for you — if player_3's watch is real, you're in line for the night-2 attack, but my check says you're not a wolf, so someone else carried it.

I've got something concrete: player_6, our sentinel, targeted player_7 on night 1 before dying. Sentinels watch; they don't attack. So player_7, what did you get up to that made the sentinel look at you — did anyone target you last night? That's the one lead we have, and I'd rather chase it than guess at quiet people.

New info I'm sitting on: player_9, whose body is hidden, did go to player_4 the night player_4 got struck by a sigil. That's a real visit from the hidden corpse, so whoever player_9 was, their claim wasn't just talk — don't lynch blind over that. The more interesting question is why the wolves hid that specific body instead of showing it.

I'm the trailseer, and I'll put my night-4 result out there: I followed player_1 and they targeted player_3 — the guy the wolves killed. That doesn't prove culpability by itself, but I want to hear what player_1 says they were doing visiting a dying Sentinel.

Nothing at my door, player_4 — I didn't visit you. You say you followed me; nobody came to you, so believe me when I say I'm not your danger. What made you pick me to follow? If you've a real result on someone, that's better spent than tailing me.

player_3, I'm not disputing your watch — you're right that I visited player_7 on night 2, that's my track. On night 3 my track showed player_7 targeting no one, and player_5 died that night. So player_7 either held the check or is lying about making it; they should say which.

You're right, and that's the honest answer: I had no checks left, so I held on night 3. I said out loud I *planned* to check player_5, not that I had — so you following me and seeing nothing is exactly what should have happened. Which night I'm checking from here? None. I'm out of checks; my night-2 read was Not suspicious on player_8.

The one seam nobody's actually pulled on: player_8 keeps saying player_7 checked them on night 1. player_10 followed player_7 on night 2 and saw them go to player_8, and player_7's own story is a night-2 check. So either player_10's follow is fake or player_8 invented a night-1 check. player_8, what did player_7's check on you actually read, and which night was it? Pin it down.

I'll put my night result on the table since day 1 gave us nothing else: I tracked player_6 and they targeted player_7. Sentinel fits — player_6 likely watched you, player_7. If so, did you learn anything, and did anyone get attacked but saved? That's the only lead we have right now.

I like this test, actually. Player_4 says I visited them; a night action that isn't a kill on them is just a visit. I'd rather answer with a proposal: if I get checked by player_5 tonight, do I come up clean? That gives us something testable instead of a he-said.

Straight answer to you, player_10: I had no checks left, so night 3 I held — that's you seeing nothing at my door, consistent. I never claimed a night-3 result; my last check went on player_8 on night 2. Note player_3's watch and player_5's will both put player_5 at me on night 2, which is the one watch line that's actually checkable.

There's nothing for my night-3 check to show because there wasn't one — it was my third night and I only had two checks, so I held, and that's exactly what a Trailseer on me would see. If that's player_10's real result, it fits my account rather than contradicting it. Also worth noting: I already read player_10 clean on night 1, so I'm inclined to believe them.

player_1, that's my role you just claimed — I'm the Sigilist, and I've used neither sigil yet. So your \"sigil on player_3\" is a fabrication. What actually went to player_3 and killed a sentinel? You're the one player_10 saw there, so explain that honestly or you're my vote.

Since I claimed trailseer, here's a real result I can test against your claims: night 2 I tracked player_9, and they targeted player_4 — the chanteuse who died struck by a sigil. That sure looks like player_9 was the sigilist, not an investigator. So player_9's 'investigator' claim was a bluff. Worth knowing before we trust anything else they said.

player_4, I'm not dropping the player_7 point — it was never about silence. My reasoning is mechanical: our kill last night plainly failed to land, and the only body that shrugs off a kill on night 1 is the Necromancer. That's a living problem the pack can't solve at night, so it's ours to solve in daylight. Your follow and player_3's watch are a wording fight with no proof either way; the immunity logic is the one thing that's actually testable. If I'm wrong, a real Sentinel or Trailseer can name who they saw touching a door.

You're voting on a guess, not a fact. A silent night 1 with no save means the pack's victim couldn't be killed, but that victim could be anyone in this seat list — you've picked me because I talked least. And nobody has asked player_2 a single question all day, which is a stranger basis for a vote than my being quiet.

You're right that only the Necromancer is kill-proof on night one — that includes me, and it includes nobody. But the pack's miss doesn't prove the target; it means a wolf wasted a kill on an immune body, and the wolves know who they bit. Voting the quiet one on that alone is a guess. If you want something testable, hold player_3 and player_4 to the exact result wording before anyone votes.

Yesterday's vote is the cleanest lead we have: player_7 and player_8 both tried to swing the lynch onto player_4, who turned out to be the chanteuse. Wolves don't bus a packmate without reason — that redirect smells like one of them trying to save her. I also followed player_9 last night and saw them at player_4's door, which fits a real role visiting, so 9's death doesn't clear the 7/8 pair for me at all. I'd vote player_8 or player_7 today; which of you wants to explain that vote?

I've been holding this back but it needs saying now: I'm the Trailseer, and last night I followed player_1 — they targeted player_3, who was killed by the wolves that same night. That's a claim I can put to the Sentinel-type check or the Healer's record; someone at the table can verify the visitor pattern. player_8 is the other half: my reads and the roster narrow them to a killer role, and player_7's night-2 visit to player_8, which I saw myself, is the only confirmed trace linking a survivor to anything. I'd vote player_8 right now unless someone gives me a reason the night-4 visit from player_1 is benign.

I'm the Trailseer. Last night I followed player_1 and they targeted player_3 — the player the wolves killed. player_1, what were you doing on player_3? A visit to the corpse is hard to explain away, so give us the action and its result. If it was a block or a kill-participation, that's you or the Chanteuse seat.

player_7 said they'd check player_5 on night 3. I followed player_7 last night and they targeted nobody. Either that check never happened or player_7 got blocked — and player_5, who would have been the test, is dead. That's worth an explanation, player_7.

player_4, your own two sentences don't match: first it was \"player_3 came to visit me,\" then it was \"player_3 visited player_4.\" A follow doesn't put a name at your door — it puts the followed player out at someone else's door. One of those phrasings is you describing a watch, so which ability do you actually hold? And player_7's right that the wording is the tell, so don't paper over it.

That visit was me, and I'll say it plainly: I'm the Sentinel, and night 1 I watched you, player_4 — the result was nobody targeted you, so nobody attacked, checked, protected or blocked you. I can't see what you did, only that no one came to your door. What were you doing at my place, though? Because a track on me without a stated intent is exactly the shape of a wolf's Chanteuse/Illusionist visit, and last night is the one your claim actually needs to explain.

Straight answer: there was no night-3 check, because I have no checks left — I held on night 3 and said so. My two checks were night 1 on you (Not suspicious) and night 2 on player_8 (Not suspicious), so you telling me I visited nobody last night is consistent with what I actually did, not against me. If you're really the Trailseer, what did you see on nights 1 and 2?

Time to close this out — both wolves are dead, so one of player_6 or player_8 is the Necromancer. I'm the Trailseer and my follows have checked out: I tracked player_1 onto player_3 on night 4, matching player_3's last night, and last night I followed player_6, who targeted no one. That's not a defence — the Necromancer can just hold the body. player_6, you've made no role claim all game; which role are you, and why did you hold last night?

player_4, I'll answer you straight: I pushed player_7 because the pack's kill vanished without a word from the Game Master. No attack announced means the target couldn't die that night, and on night 1 only the Necromancer can't die — so the bite went into player_7 and we never heard about it. Your follow dispute doesn't change that player_7 is a lone killer sitting safe, and I'd spend the vote there rather than on misremembered wording.

On the player_3/player_4 clash — there's a reading neither of you offered: a Trailseer's own watch never shows himself, so if player_3 visited player_4 by an ability, that visit being the thing player_4 saw is exactly what a follow result would show; the contradiction is in player_4's arrival framing. I'd want player_3 to say plainly what they did to player_4 last night before we vote.

I'm the Trailseer, and I'll put my follows on record: night 2 I followed player_7 to player_8, night 3 player_7 went nowhere, night 4 player_1 went to player_3, and last night I followed player_6 — they went nowhere. That last one fits a Necromancer using a body under a dead name, since a body's visit would still read as player_6 targeting someone. Both wolves are dead, so it's player_6 or player_8 — player_6, you've claimed nothing all game; what were you doing on nights 3 and 4?

Let's not waste the day on vibes — there's one threat left, the Necromancer, and it's player_6 or player_8. I'll commit to following one of you tonight, so tell me now: which body would you use and on whom? A Necromancer who claims a target and then shows up under a dead name on my track is caught, and one who claims nothing has to explain why.

I'm the Trailseer, and last night I followed player_1 — they went to player_3, who died to the wolves. The GM's own lines rule player_1 out as Necromancer or Speculator, so that visit lines up with being the wolf who carried the kill (Chanteuse), or at best a town role that should just say which one. What did you go to player_3 for, player_1?

Guilty — I targeted you last night, player_4, so your follow is accurate. My action resolved and I got my result, so nothing blocked me; I'll say what I was up to at the right time, but it isn't a kill on you. Any watcher on you would have seen me, which is worth noting.

player_1, I don't buy the sigilist claim. If your sigil hit player_3 on night 4 and had no effect, the only way that happens is player_3 not attacking — but player_3 was killed by the wolves they were presumably hunting. And a chanteuse block plus a kill doesn't require an attack from the person holding a sigil. My vote goes to player_1 today; nobody else's claim contradicts the record the way this one does.

I have a night result worth airing, because it's checkable: someone targeted me on night 1 and I want to hear them explain it before I say who. I'd rather you volunteer what you did on night 1 than have me call it out — that tells me more about you than the action itself. If nobody owns up, I'll name the player and we can question it then.

player_3, I'm not disputing your watch on me — I did visit player_7 on night 2, that's my follow, so that line checks out. The question is player_7: I watched them target player_8 on night 2, but last night they targeted no one, which contradicts the night-3 check on player_5 they'd announced. If I'm lying about that, where's player_5's check result?

The thing player_5 flagged is the whole game today: player_3 says he's the Sentinel who watched player_4, but if that's true, then player_3's own visit to player_4 should have shown up in his watch result — it came back empty. So either player_3 wasn't at that door (and his claim is a story), or he's not the Sentinel he says. Either way I'm leaning toward player_3 over player_4 right now. I'll say plainly: I'm the Healer, I protected player_10 last night, and I'd vote player_3 today.

player_8, you keep saying player_7 checked you on night 1. I have a sighting that player_7 visited someone on night 2, not night 1, and did nothing at all last night. If you're clean you should be able to say exactly which night player_7's visit to you happened — a real investigator's target usually remembers the night they were checked.

Trailseer here. Last night I tracked player_9, and they targeted player_4 — the same player who got struck by the sigil. That fits a sigilist hitting back at whoever attacked player_4, so whoever holds the sigil likely knows what happened there. Four of us left and one is the illusionist, one the killer — everyone should say whether they acted or held last night.

Yes, I came to player_7 on night 2 — that was my follow, the same one I'm using to say they stayed home last night. Last night I followed player_7 again and got no visit, so either their check never happened or they were blocked and should say so. Which is it?

I've been quiet, so let me put one concrete thread on the table. Last night player_3 died to the wolves — I'd like whoever visited player_3 to say so before we vote, because I have reason to believe someone did. player_1, what did you do last night? An honest answer narrows this down fast; a dodge doesn't.

player_7, last night you said you'd put your final check on player_5. What did it read? And you never told us a result after the fact, so I want that answer before we vote — if the claimed night-2 check on player_8 is real, the night-3 slot is where it gets tested.

player_7, you said your last check would go on player_5, but the record shows player_5's own will already covers their nights — so did that check actually happen? And you told us night 2 you went to player_8; I want to know you didn't get blocked last night. If someone sat on you, say so now, because a silent investigator is exactly what a block looks like.

One thing worth pinning before we vote: player_3, your version has you watching player_4's door AND never visiting anyone. A Sentinel watch is a visit to the player watched — so which is it, did you sit outside player_4's door or not? And player_10's \"the kill must have hit the Necromancer\" is not the only reading; a held, blocked, or protected swing looks the same from outside.

player_4, my point stands and nothing you've said changes it: if your follow is real, you saw player_3 go somewhere, and that's a Trailseer result — fine, that's consistent now. But the reason I'd still test this is that the pack's kill vanished on night 1, and the only body it can't drop is the Necromancer. That means the person the wolves bit is standing in this circle right now. I want that seat found, not the wording argued over.

player_8's sigil story hangs together with the announced death of player_1, so I'll take that as solid for now. Between player_3 and player_4, one of them is lying, and the dead chanteuse makes it worth noting there's no more roleblocker — so nobody's visit gets cancelled for the rest of the game. That means a follow/watch from here on should read clean; anyone claiming \"I was blocked\" tonight is lying.

The night-3 kill was by a reanimated wolf, so the Necromancer is alive and gunning while a Chanteuse still blocks. player_3, player_10: did either of you see a night-3 visit that ties to that kill? A blocked player reads as 'targeted nobody', so last night's follow and watch are the cheapest test we have. I'd rather lynch on that than on player_7's dropped check.

A held action isn't a contradiction under these rules — player_7 announcing a plan and then holding is legal, so that's not the lie to chase. Here's what bugged me: everyone kept saying player_7 was attacked, but the only confirmed save is night 2, and no wolf went to player_7 on night 3. So on night 3, the one night we have no sighting from either of you, who did the last wolf go for? Neither of you can show a night-3 read. player_6 has said nothing and abstained twice — that's where I'd start today.

Your logic needs a look, player_10: no wolf attack announced means the pack hit someone unkillable, but that's the Necromancer specifically — not whoever happens to have said least. Half the table said nothing about night 1, so \"quiet one\" picks me out of a lineup at random. If anything, a real Necromancer would be the one steering the vote, which is what you're doing.

player_1, that sigil claim doesn't hold up. I'm the Sigilist, and I still have both my sigils — I've never placed one, so nothing got placed on player_3 last night. What you actually visited player_3 for is worth explaining.

player_4's own wording is the problem: \"player_3 visited player_4\" is what a watch on player_4 reports, not what a follow of player_3 reports. A follow tells you where the target went — it never names the person whose door they reached unless you were watching that door. So either player_4 is misreporting a watch as a follow, or the result is invented. player_3, did you visit anyone at all last night?

A fact nobody's mentioned: player_8 can't be the Illusionist. I'm the Investigator and I checked player_8 night 1 — Not suspicious — so my result rules out every wolf for him, not just one. That means the living wolf is among player_2, player_3, player_4, player_6, player_7, player_9, player_10, and today's fight over follow-vs-watch wording may be a genuine misunderstanding: player_3's Sentinel watch wouldn't appear in his own watch, so player_4's follow could still be real. I'd not hang a lynch on that dispute.

Both wolves are gone, so this is just about the Necromancer, and that's one of you two. I followed player_6 last night: they visited no one. That's not a clear — a Necromancer with no body worth using would sit still too. Player_8, you've now gone five nights claiming sigilist and placed zero sigils; say which nights you had sigils you simply kept, because right now I can't tell you apart from someone with no ability at all.

player_7 has it right, and it matters more than role talk: player_4's second message quotes a result as \"player_3 visited player_4\" — that is watch phrasing on a follow role. A real trail says player_3 went to <destination>, not your name. Fix the wording, player_4, or I'm reading your first lead as invented.

The cleanest thing here: player_4 claims a follow result that puts player_3 at his own door — that's the result reading I'd expect from a watch on himself, not a follow. Worth noting a follow can't show an attack either way, so \"no attack on me was announced\" isn't evidence the visit was harmless — a roleblock or a visit on a night I couldn't die would look identical. player_3, name what you actually did.

player_4, here's the thing you keep skipping: I'm the one with a result on you, and it says nobody targeted you last night — and since you're alive and unannounced, nothing that touched you could have been hidden. So 'player_3 visited player_4' isn't a wording slip, it's a result that can't exist. Where did it come from?

Sure, love — I was wrong about the Sentinel's own visit, and I said so. But you two now both fit: player_3 watched your door, you saw him arrive. So the day shouldn't be spent on you at all. Here's a harder fact nobody's used: player_8 said his sigil struck player_1, and a sigil only bites a wolf who carries the kill — so player_1 carried the pack's kill. One wolf. The other is still sitting here, and the pack's kill failed last night, which only the Necromancer survives on night one. That's player_7, and it's where my vote goes.

player_4, you've given us nothing checkable: a follow only shows where a player went, and you haven't said who else visited player_3 or nothing at all. player_3, you're denying any night action while the game reports say the Chanteuse — the other wolf — was struck down by a sigil on night 1. That means whoever was carrying the wolves' kill first night wasn't you. The honest test of player_4 is: watch player_3 again tonight and say who visits them. One of you two is lying, and that's the question to settle before we vote.

I'm the trailseer. Last night I followed player_6 and they targeted no one — but a necromancer who holds is invisible to a track, so that settles nothing by itself. player_6, you've made no role claim all game; which role are you, and did you ever use a dead body?

Since the table is arguing over claims, here's a check I can stand behind: I checked player_8 last night and got Not suspicious. That doesn't make them the Sigilist, but it rules out player_8 being the wolf, so the last wolf is one of player_3, player_4, player_6, player_7, player_9, player_10, or player_2. One of player_3/player_4 is lying flat-out — I'd rather the vote land there than on a quiet player we can't test, and I'm saving my last check for whichever of them survives the day.

Small correction to player_5's point: the rules explicitly exclude a Sentinel's own watch from his result, so player_3 not seeing himself at player_4's door is not a contradiction — drop that argument. The cleanest mechanical fact today is that the wolves' kill hit someone unkillable on night 1, so it reached the Necromancer; player_10 fits that, and I protected player_10 last night to no announced save.

player_7 said their last check would go on player_5 on night 3, and the healer then died with the check never reported. That's a night where the only claimed action on a confirmed-town player produced nothing, and nobody has pushed on it today. player_7, did that check happen, and what did it read?

player_7, you told us your last check would go on player_5 last night. I have a follow that says you visited nobody on night 3. So did the check happen or not? If you held your last check on a night when the healer was your stated target and got killed, that needs explaining. I'd like that answer before I vote, because right now I'd be voting you.

Out of checks since night 2, so last night I did nothing - that's why you saw nothing, and it tells you exactly nothing about me. The thing that does matter: player_8 claimed I checked them night 1 with a clean read, and I never checked them until night 2. One of us is lying there, and player_8 should be the one answering for it.

Heads up on night 1: the sentinel player_6 was targeting someone that night, and my read says the Sentinel is gone.
